identity.name: Nautilus
identity.one_liner: 170 double-signed steel Nautilus with a Tiffany Blue lacquer dial; piece No. 1 sold for $6.5 million at Phillips.

comps.condition: piece No. 1 of 170, single-lot charity sale

provenance_events.person_or_event: Phillips single-lot charity sale, New York
provenance_events.description: The first 5711/1A-018 sold for $6,503,500 including fees, roughly 124 times its $52,635 retail price, with proceeds to The Nature Conservancy. It closed the 5711 story eleven months after the reference was discontinued.

narrative.story: Patek's send-off for the 5711 and a nod to 170 years of retail partnership with Tiffany & Co.: 170 pieces with a Tiffany Blue lacquer dial, double-signed on dial and caseback, allocated only through Tiffany boutiques in December 2021. Piece No. 1 went straight to Phillips as a single-lot charity sale and made $6.5 million, the number that came to stand for the entire 2021 watch bubble.
narrative.collector_notes: The dial and caseback double stamp is the whole game; paperwork tracing the Tiffany allocation matters more here than on any standard Nautilus. Later examples have changed hands far below the charity result, which was a one-off number with a philanthropic premium built in.
